metadata.title: fix(auth): resolve aware vs naive datetime comparison for SQLite lockout
metadata.author: cafalchio

description: ## 🔗 Related Issue Closes #3401 --- ## 📝 Summary SQLite stores `datetime` values without timezone info (naive datetimes), while PostgreSQL preserves timezone-aware datetimes. This caused a `TypeError` when comparing a naive `locked_until` value against the timezone-aware result of `utc_now()`, which silently broke the Admin UI users list whenever any user had a non-null `locked_until` — showing zero users instead of the full list. **Root cause:** `is_account_locked()` in `db.py` was comparing `utc_now()` (timezone-aware) directly against `self.locked_until` (naive on SQLite), raising a `TypeError` that propagated up and caused the user list to render empty. **Fix:** - `EmailUser.is_account_locked()` now normalises a naive `locked_until` to UTC before comparison, making it safe on both SQLite and PostgreSQL. - `admin.py` and `schemas.py` now delegate lock status to `user.is_account_locked()` instead of duplicating the comparison inline — eliminating the two divergent call sites that had the same bug. --- ## 🏷️ Type of Change - [X] Bug fix - [ ] Feature / Enhancement - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Chore (deps, CI, tooling) --- ## 🧪 Verification | Check | Command | Status | |---------------------------|-----------------|--------| | Lint suite | `make lint` | | | Unit tests | `make test` | | | Coverage ≥ 80% | `make coverage` | | --- ## ✅ Checklist - [✅] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`) - [✅] Tests added/updated for changes - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [✅] No secrets or credentials committed --- ## 📓 Notes **Affected files:** - `mcpgateway/db.py` — `is_account_locked()` normalises naive datetimes from SQLite before comparison - `mcpgateway/admin.py` — `_render_user_card_html` uses `user.is_account_locked()` instead of inline comparison - `mcpgateway/schemas.py` — `EmailUserResponse.from_email_user()` uses `user.is_account_locked()` instead of inline comparison - `tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_db.py` — new tests for naive and aware datetime paths in `is_account_locked()` - `tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_admin.py` — mock objects updated with `is_account_locked` method

commits.message:
fix(auth): use is_account_locked() in template data path to fix remaining naive datetime bug

The admin_users_partial_html template data builder at admin.py:6863 still
had the old inline `locked_until > utc_now()` comparison that raises
TypeError on SQLite (naive vs aware datetime). Replace with
user_obj.is_account_locked() to match the fix already applied to
_render_user_card_html and schemas.py.

Update SimpleNamespace mocks in admin_users_partial_html tests to include
the is_account_locked method now required by both rendering paths.

Closes #3401
Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix(auth): remove write-on-read mutation from is_account_locked()

Stop assigning the normalized UTC-aware value back to self.locked_until
in is_account_locked(). This method is called from GET/list/serialization
paths (admin_users_partial_html, EmailUserResponse.from_email_user) that
commit their sessions, so mutating the ORM field turned read-only
endpoints into writes.

Use a local variable for the comparison instead, matching the pattern in
TeamInvitation.is_expired() at db.py:1969.

Also fix test naive datetimes to use UTC-based values
(datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)) instead of
datetime.now(), which is timezone-dependent and could fail on non-UTC
runners.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix(auth): snapshot locked_until after is_account_locked() and add regression tests

Reorder field captures in _render_user_card_html, admin_users_partial_html,
and EmailUserResponse.from_email_user to call is_account_locked() before
snapshotting locked_until and failed_login_attempts. This ensures that
when a lock has expired and the method clears those fields, the rendered
output reflects the cleared state rather than showing stale values.

Add three regression tests that exercise the real _render_user_card_html
and EmailUserResponse.from_email_user with actual EmailUser objects
carrying naive locked_until datetimes (simulating SQLite), covering
active lock, expired lock, and field-clearing scenarios.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
